text:
gabi: onboarding hit a weird ImportError on macOS runners: `ImportError: /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_ext/_native.cpython-311-darwin.so: wrong ELF class` even though locally on linux everything is fine.
noah: that sounds like a wheel built for linux (ELF) being installed on mac (Mach-O). How are you installing in CI?
gabi: sample-app CI does `poetry export -f requirements.txt -o reqs.txt` then `pip install -r reqs.txt`. Our internal index served a wheel named like `redwood_ext-0.2.1-py3-none-any.whl` but inside it had a linux-built .so.
ryan: if the wheel has a platform-specific extension it should include platform tag not `none-any`. Sounds like the packager accidentally named the file wrong. Is this from a local build or from the artifact registry?
gabi: the build pipeline produced a wheel on linux and we pushed to internal index as a generic wheel by mistake (CI plumbing bug). Poetry export didn't mark the dep as platform-specific so pip happily picked the wheel on mac runner.
ci-bot: job #9801 failed on step "pip install -r reqs.txt"  https://ci.internal/9801/logs
mira: short term: add a CI step before install to assert wheel platform tags. Example: ```python -c "import pkgutil, zipfile, sys, sysconfig; print(sys.platform)"``` or download the wheel and inspect `zipinfo dist/*.whl | head` to check .so path and filename.
noah: also fix: in packaging pipeline, ensure wheels built on linux are pushed with correct tag or as manylinux wheels; or push platform-specific wheels to platform-specific repos.gabi: quick workaround I used: force pip to prefer sdist build on mac runner: `pip install --no-binary redwood-ext -r reqs.txt` which compiled the extension natively. It's slower but unblocks.
ryan: long term: change sample-app CI to use `python -m build` in a clean builder so we can test install semantics across platforms: `python -m build -w -o dist; pip install dist/*.whl` in a mac runner test lane. Add a packaging smoke test to catch mismatched wheel tags.
mira: filing SDK issue with repro and recommended fixes: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-python/issues/358. Also adding onboarding note: "When exporting from poetry to pip, double-check that internal registry stores correct platform tags for binary wheels; prefer sdist constraints or build wheels per-platform."
gabi: thanks. temporary CI changes pushed to sample-app PR 204 to force sdist on mac and run the inspect step. CI green on branch. will follow up when infra evicts the bad wheel. :white_check_mark:
